newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Active Nigerian share trade as brewer turns buy.
newsitem.headline: Active Nigerian share trade as brewer turns buy.

text.p: Trading was heavy on the Nigerian stock market on Monday as investors returned to buy Nigerian Breweries shares which they have shunned for most of the year.
The all-share index rose to 6644.86 from 6635.21 on Friday.
Nigerian Breweries rose five kobo to 10.25 naira as buyers outnumbered sellers, traders said.
"It shows that the stock has bottomed out," one trader said.
Demand for food companies was strong, pushing up Nestle 60 kobo to 39.20 naira. Union Dicon was 50 kobo up at 38.50 naira while Nigerian Tobacco Company rose three kobo to 3.18 naira.

Oil stocks advanced steadily with National Oil reaping the most with a 30 kobo rise to 38.10 naira. African Petroleum and Unipetrol both garnered 20 kobo to close, respectively at 36.20 naira and 46.00 naira.
Demand for cement and construction shares remained high. West African Portland Cement closed at 37.50 naira and Ashaka Cement at 19.50 naira, each 30 kobo better.
Cappa and D'Alberto was 10 kobo up at 9.00 naira, the same as G.Cappa at 9.50 naira. Impresit Bakolori was five kobo up at 2.40 naira and Costain rose three kobo to 1.95 naira.
But large volumes on offer caused Union Bank to slump to 7.20 naira, down 10 kobo. Chemical and Allied Products was down by a similar figure at 7.10 naira.
Other lossers were Cadbury, down two kobo at 25.98 naira, conglomerate UAC five lower at 9.35 naira and stationery firm Thomas Wyatt, down five kobo at 7.00 naira. ($1=80 naira)
